'When this hits a hero' = TRIGGERED ON_HIT (an Action - Attack is not an ATTACK_REACTION) + ATTACK_TARGET_IS_HERO ('a hero').

Flip half: FLIP_MATCHING with an object target - _compile_object_target filters the opponent's arsenal with CARD_IS_FACE_DOWN, asks the EFFECT CONTROLLER to choose 1 (mandatory-if-available: an empty pool returns [] without prompting, satisfying release note 1), and flips via is_public/face_down. record_as is informational; nothing downstream reads it.

Banish half: BANISH from the opponent's ARSENAL with a filter riding the target dict (_hand_card_filter compiles raw DSL condition specs, ANDed): it IS an Action (SUBTYPE_IN 'Action'), is NOT an Attack (NOT around SUBTYPE_IN 'Attack' - Attack is a subtype, Action is a type, and 'non-attack action' is two claims about one card), and is face up (CARD_IS_FACE_UP), per release note 2. Mandatory-if-available: the handler breaks silently when no candidate matches. Exactly one is taken (amount 1). It runs unconditionally after the flip - release note 3 - and because the flip happens first and sets is_public, the just-flipped card legitimately joins the banish pool but does not have to be the one taken (release note 4).

DEVIATION (handler-level, flagged not fixed): BANISH's choice prompt goes to _ask_player(state, tid) - the ZONE OWNER - whereas CR-wise the effect's controller chooses which of the opponent's arsenal cards is banished. Filtering is exact (only legal candidates are offered); only the chooser differs. Fixing it means teaching the shared BANISH handler a chooser param - a generic engine change, out of scope for a draft.

The triage list suggested LOOK_AT + SELECT_FROM_REF + FLIP_REF + BANISH_REF for this card. That path was rejected deliberately: LOOK_AT's zone filter supports only keyword/subtype/face_down (no card-type key), so the ref pool could not be narrowed to non-attack actions and SELECT_FROM_REF would offer illegal candidates. The object-target route reuses the full condition vocabulary instead.
